subtitle: On the rock of Girnar, a Saka king carves war, wisdom and water into stone

panels.shot: low-angle wide of the Girnar rock face with Rudradaman I standing before it, mountains and clouds looming
panels.action: Rudradaman I stands in profile before the towering rock of Girnar, cloak caught in the wind, one hand resting on a sheathed sword, the other extended toward the blank stone, as rugged hills and dark monsoon clouds frame him.

dialogue.text: On the ancient rock of Girnar, Rudradaman the Saka carves his boast: of wars won, kinship spared, storms survived, and a lake restored. What truth does this stone remember of him?

i18n.hi: गिरनार की पुरानी चट्टान पर शक रुद्रदामन अपना घमंड उकेरता है – जीती जंगें, बचाए नाते, झेली आँधियाँ, और फिर से जगा सरोवर। यह पत्थर उसके बारे में क्या सच याद रखता है?

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of western India with map-like overlay feel, slowly pushing in toward Girinagara
panels.action: A sweeping view of western India shows dusty plains, winding rivers and trade routes, with Girnar’s dark peak rising near the coast as tiny caravans and ships hint at busy commerce.

dialogue.text: In the second century of the Common Era, western India was a crossroads. Saka chiefs, Satavahana kings, old clans and caravan towns all pulled at the same lands between sea and plateau.

i18n.hi: ईस्वी की दूसरी सदी में पश्चिमी भारत चौराहा था। शक सरदार, सातवाहन राजा, पुराने कुल और काफ़िला-नगर सब सागर और पठार के बीच की धरती खींच रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Rudradaman I in a coin-engraver’s workshop, slow push-in
panels.action: Rudradaman I, in regal attire with a diadem, stands in a mint-like workshop, watching as an artisan engraves his profile and titles onto a gleaming round coin laid on a small anvil.

dialogue.text: Among the Saka Western Kshatrapas, one name begins to appear in silver and copper: Mahakshatrapa Rudradaman, lord of Girinagara, his face pressed into coins that travel from port to plateau.

i18n.hi: शक पच्छिमी क्षत्रपों में एक नाम चाँदी–ताँबे पर उभरता है – महाक्षत्रप रुद्रदामन, गिरिनगर का स्वामी, जिसका चेहरा सिक्कों पर छपकर बंदरगाह से पठार तक घूमता है।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of a court, with Rudradaman I seated amid scribes and learned men
panels.action: In a pillared hall, Rudradaman I sits on a low throne, leaning forward as Brahmana scholars and scribes recite, while palm-leaf manuscripts, zithers and a grammar text lie arranged before them.

dialogue.text: His own inscription will later claim more than war. It praises a king trained in grammar, music, logic and literature, who delights in polished speech as much as in the ring of steel.

i18n.hi: उसकी अपनी अभिलेख सिर्फ जंग नहीं गिनती। वह राजा की तारीफ़ करती है जो व्याकरण, संगीत, तर्क और साहित्य में दीक्षित है, जिसे चमकीली वाणी उतनी ही सुहाती है जितनी लोहे की टंकार।

panels.shot: medium shot of Rudradaman I listening to a scribe recite Sanskrit prose, close on his focused expression
panels.action: Rudradaman I, eyes narrowed in concentration, listens as a court scribe recites a flowing Sanskrit passage, while another scribe carefully inscribes characters onto a palm leaf with a stylus.

dialogue.text: The Junagadh inscription, composed in ornate Sanskrit prose, calls him a master of language. Its style shines, but the stone itself is silent on who chose each word.

i18n.hi: जुनागढ़ अभिलेख, अलंकृत संस्कृत गद्य में रचा, उसे भाषा का उस्ताद कहता है। शैली दमकती है, पर पत्थर चुप है कि हर शब्द किसने चुना।

panels.shot: wide shot of the Sudarshana Lake and old Mauryan dam at the foot of Girnar, calm before a storm
panels.action: A serene reservoir stretches at the foot of Girnar’s slopes, held by an old stone-and-earth embankment, as farmers, cattle and small boats move around its shores under a hazy sky.

dialogue.text: Below Girnar lies the Sudarshana Lake, first dammed under the Mauryas. Ashoka’s men once built here; Rudradaman’s age inherits their work, and with it, the burden of keeping water in a fickle land.

i18n.hi: गिरनार के नीचे है सुदर्शन झील, जो पहली बार मौर्यों के समय बाँधी गई। यहाँ कभी अशोक के लोग बने; रुद्रदामन का युग उसी काम और उसी चंचल धरती में पानी थामने का बोझ विरासत में पाता है।

panels.shot: dramatic wide shot of a monsoon storm breaking over the dam, with Rudradaman I observing from a distance
panels.action: Dark monsoon clouds burst over Girnar as torrents of rain hammer the Sudarshana dam; Rudradaman I, cloaked, stands on a rocky rise with attendants, watching waves crash and spray leap over the embankment.

dialogue.text: Then the sky turns. The inscription tells of a fierce storm that lashes Girnar, sending floods roaring at the old embankment. Earth shakes, masonry groans, and the lake that fed fields threatens to break loose.

i18n.hi: फिर आसमान बदलता है। अभिलेख बताता है भयानक आँधी का जो गिरनार को कोड़े मारती है, बाढ़ों को पुराने बाँध पर दे दौड़ाती है। धरती हिलती, गारा कराहता, और खेतों को पालने वाली झील टूट भागने को होती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Rudradaman I in council with engineers and officials, pointing toward the damaged dam
panels.action: In rain-slicked clothes under a temporary awning, Rudradaman I confers with engineers and officers, one holding a rough sketch of the broken embankment, as he gestures decisively toward the flooded valley.

dialogue.text: Rudradaman’s prasasti says he orders the lake restored at his own cost. No levy, no enforced labor, it proclaims, only the king’s treasury and will turned toward rebuilding what storm tore apart.

i18n.hi: रुद्रदामन की प्राशस्ती कहती है कि वह झील की मरम्मत अपने ख़र्च से कराता है। न कर, न बेगार – बस राजा का ख़ज़ाना और इरादा, जो तूफ़ान से टूटे को फिर से जोड़ने में लगता है।

panels.shot: wide shot of laborers and artisans rebuilding the dam, with Rudradaman I overseeing from a parapet
panels.action: Hundreds of laborers haul stone blocks and ram earth as artisans fit dressed masonry; Rudradaman I stands on a temporary parapet, watching calmly while Girnar looms behind and water gleams in the half-filled basin.

dialogue.text: Stone by stone, they raise a stronger embankment. The king’s name binds itself to the reservoir’s new life, tying Saka rule not only to conquest, but to the steady weight of water held and fields saved.

i18n.hi: पत्थर दर पत्थर वे मज़बूत बाँध उठाते हैं। झील की नई जान पर राजा का नाम खुद जाता है, शक सत्ता को सिर्फ फ़तह से नहीं, सँभाले हुए पानी और बचे हुए खेतों की ठोस वज़न से बाँधते हुए।

panels.shot: dynamic wide shot of Rudradaman I on horseback leading armored cavalry across an open plain
panels.action: Rudradaman I, armored and stern, rides at the head of a wedge of cavalry over a dusty plain, pennons streaming, as lines of infantry and elephants march in the background under a hot, pale sun.

dialogue.text: But the same inscription that celebrates the dam also sharpens his sword. It calls him a conqueror who defeats many chiefs, a rider who can loose arrows from horseback and split ranks with his cavalry.

i18n.hi: पर वही लेख जो बाँध की वाहवाही करता है, उसकी तलवार भी तेज़ करता है। वह उसे विजेता कहता है जो कई नायकों को हराता है, घुड़सवार जो काठी से तीर बरसा सकता है और घुड़सवार दस्ता से पंक्तियाँ चीर देता है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Rudradaman I facing a resolute Yaudheya envoy on a battlefield edge
panels.action: On the edge of a battlefield, Rudradaman I sits mounted, facing a standing Yaudheya envoy in simple armor, behind whom faint ranks of Yaudheya warriors can be seen refusing to lower their spears.

dialogue.text: Of the Yaudheyas, an ancient republican clan, the stone uses stark words: they refused his overlordship, it says, and so he, by force, destroyed them when they would not submit.

i18n.hi: यौधेयों, उस प्राचीन गणकुल, के लिए पत्थर सख़्त शब्द चुनता है – वे उसकी अधीनता नहीं मानते, वह कहता है, तो उसने ज़ोर से उन्हें मिटा दिया जब वे झुकने से इनकार रहे।

panels.shot: wide shot of clashing battle lines with dust clouds, without close-up violence
panels.action: Two dense armies surge toward each other on a plain, dust clouds rising as spears lower and war elephants advance; Rudradaman I’s banner stands out above his compact central line.

dialogue.text: No gore stains the stone, but its boast is clear. Here Rudradaman’s own record ties his name to the breaking of a resisting people, setting this victory among the other titles that crown him.

i18n.hi: पत्थर पर खून नहीं, पर शेखी साफ़ है। यहाँ रुद्रदामन का अपना ब्यौरा उसके नाम को एक डटे हुए लोगों को तोड़ने से जोड़ता है, इस जीत को उसकी और उपाधियों के बीच सजाकर।

panels.shot: medium shot of Rudradaman I facing a Satavahana king in armor, both poised but restrained
panels.action: Rudradaman I, armored and composed, stands across a small no-man’s-land from a Satavahana king, both flanked by guards, their expressions tense yet controlled, as distant armies hold position behind them.

dialogue.text: The inscription also recalls another rival: a Satakarni of the Satavahanas. Twice, it claims, Rudradaman defeated him in fair fight, yet twice chose not to destroy him utterly.

i18n.hi: अभिलेख एक और प्रतिद्वंदी याद करता है – सातवाहनों का एक सातकर्णि। दो बार, वह दावा करता है, रुद्रदामन ने उसे सामने की लड़ाई में हराया, फिर भी दो बार उसे पूरी तरह मिटाने से बचा।

panels.shot: closer medium shot focusing on Rudradaman I’s face as he signals restraint, with the Satavahana king in background
panels.action: Rudradaman I raises his hand in a measured gesture of halt, his expression firm but not vengeful, while the distant figure of the Satavahana king is seen withdrawing with his retinue across the field.

dialogue.text: Why? Because of kinship, the stone explains. Their houses were linked by marriage, and the record makes this restraint another jewel in his crown, set alongside courage and skill in arms.

i18n.hi: क्यों? पत्थर कहता है – रिश्तेदारी। उनके घर ब्याह से जुड़े थे, और यह रिकॉर्ड इस रुकावट को उसके मुकुट में एक और रत्न बनाता है, वीरता और हथियार-कौशल के साथ जड़ा हुआ।

panels.shot: interior shot of Rudradaman I in court, receiving tribute from various chiefs and traders
panels.action: In his audience hall, Rudradaman I sits as chiefs in diverse dress and merchants with bolts of cloth and sacks of coins bow, while attendants stack tribute and scribes record transactions on palm leaves.

dialogue.text: With rivals checked and routes secured, his authority stretches over Saurashtra and Malwa. Coins bearing his titles move with trade, and the dam at Sudarshana feeds fields that help fill his treasuries.

i18n.hi: दुश्मन दबे और राहें सुरक्षित, उसकी सत्ता सौराष्ट्र और मालवा तक फैलती है। उसके खिताब वाले सिक्के व्यापार के साथ चलते हैं, और सुदर्शन बाँध के खेत उसके ख़ज़ाने भरने में मदद करते हैं।

panels.shot: low-angle close-up of the Girnar rock face as masons carve the inscription, Rudradaman I silhouetted above
panels.action: Masons balance on scaffolding, chisels biting into the curved face of the Girnar rock, carving crisp Sanskrit characters, while Rudradaman I stands above them on the slope, a dark silhouette against the sky.

dialogue.text: At Girnar, under old Mauryan lines, his men cut new letters. They weave genealogy, learning, war, mercy and public works into a single flowing prose, anchoring his memory beside Ashoka’s.

i18n.hi: गिरनार पर, पुराने मौर्य लेखों के नीचे, उसके लोग नए अक्षर काटते हैं। वे वंशावली, विद्या, जंग, दया और लोक-कार्य को एक बहती गद्य-धारा में पिरोते हैं, उसकी याद को अशोक के बगल में गाड़ते हुए।

panels.shot: close-up of the freshly carved inscription, with Rudradaman I’s reflection faintly visible in a nearby pool
panels.action: The camera lingers on neat rows of freshly carved inscription on the rock, edges still sharp, while in a rain-filled hollow nearby a faint reflection of Rudradaman I’s face shimmers.

dialogue.text: Scholars later will prize this record as one of the earliest long Sanskrit inscriptions, a polished royal voice that lets a Saka ruler speak of himself in a language that will shape courts for centuries.

i18n.hi: विद्वान आगे चलकर इस लेख को शुरुआती लम्बे संस्कृत अभिलेखों में गिनेंगे – एक तराशा हुआ शाही स्वर, जिसमें एक शक शासक अपने को उस भाषा में बोलता है जो सदियों दरबार गढ़ेगी।

panels.shot: wide present-day style shot imagining later travelers reading the rock, with Rudradaman I as a faded ghostly figure in background
panels.action: Later travelers in simple garments stand before the weathered rock, tracing the old letters with their eyes, while a faint, translucent figure of Rudradaman I lingers above the inscription, half-merged with the stone.

dialogue.text: Rudradaman’s own words, carved in stone, leave little room for legend. They preserve both the dam and the destroyed, the spared rival and the flood tamed, letting later ages weigh his fame for themselves.

i18n.hi: रुद्रदामन के अपने शब्द, पत्थर में खुदे, दंतकथा को कम जगह देते हैं। वे बाँध और उजड़े हुए, बख़्शे प्रतिद्वंदी और बाँधी बाढ़ – सब बचा रखते हैं, ताकि बाद की उम्रें खुद उसका मान-अपमान तौलें।

subtitle_i18n.en: On the rock of Girnar, a Saka king carves war, wisdom and water into stone
subtitle_i18n.hi: गिरनार की चट्टान पर एक शक राजा जंग, ज्ञान और पानी पत्थर में खोदता है
